children: Indian shares opened a tad higher on Tuesday, following gains in Wall Street and Asian stocks, as easing crude prices and Treasury yields supported investor sentiment ahead of potential US-Iran talks at the UN General Assembly this week.
rose 0.26% to 23,468.08, while the BSE Sensex
added 0.18% to 74,981.91, as of 9:15 a.m. IST.
Fifteen of the 16 major sectors logged gains at the open. The broader small-caps
hovered around $101 per barrel, after dropping for four consecutive sessions until Monday, while the benchmark US 10-year yield fell.
The Nasdaq notched a record high overnight, and Asian stocks mirrored gains in the morning trade. MSCI's broadest index for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) rose 1.5%.

Iran and the US exchanged threats on Sunday, though President Donald Trump said he would be open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is expected to be in New York this week for the UN General Assembly.
